subject: 654F0A9EF8A7EEFDC749F4577396E5B5
introduction: “The friends of God must assist each other, and in assistance be greater than all the other communities of the world.” The guide collects ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s encouragement of every kind of organized care: famine relief, orphans’ funds set aside from a village storehouse, schools supported from abroad, and the hospital, hospice and homes that are to surround each house of worship. The law of Israel left the corners of the field and laid up a tithe for the stranger, the fatherless and the widow; the first church appointed seven men to make its care dependable; the Qur’an writes giving into its definition of righteousness; Mencius extends the family’s care outward; Tocqueville saw Americans forming associations for everything. The critics of charity are here too, and they are not hard-hearted: Wilde wants poverty made impossible, Thoreau wants the root struck, and Blake suspects pity of needing the poor. The Gospel’s secret alms ask what an organization does to the giver.
questions: Israel’s tithe, the seven of Acts and the village storehouse of reading 15 all make care a standing arrangement. What does an institution add to individual kindness, and what can it lose?
Wilde wants a society in which poverty is impossible; Blake suspects that pity depends on there being poor. Which readings look beyond relief toward the causes of want?
“Irrespective of colour and race.” Paul says “especially unto them who are of the household of faith”. How do the readings order care for one’s own community and care for all?
The dependencies of the house of worship are a hospital, a school, a hospice. What is being said by building them around a temple?
“Let not thy left hand know.” How can a society that publishes its accounts keep the spirit of that saying?

outside.why: The friends “must assist each other, and in assistance be greater than all the other communities”. The multitude of them that believed were of one heart and of one soul: neither said any of them that ought of the things which he possessed was his own.
Paul gives the order of care: let us do good unto all men, especially unto them who are of the household of faith.
To know that helping the poor is good is not yet to help. If one say, Be ye warmed and filled, and give them not those things which are needful, what doth it profit?
Charitable funds from an endowment are to be distributed among the poor. Thou shalt open thine hand wide unto thy brother, to thy poor, and to thy needy.
“Its charities will be dispensed irrespective of colour and race.” The neighbour in the parable is a foreigner who had compassion.
Care for poor children is “of greatest service”. Pure religion and undefiled before God is this, to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction.
A relief society served through famine. When a great dearth was foretold, the disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief.
“The poor of this world suffer: we should care for them.” The poor shall never cease out of the land: therefore I command thee, saying, Thou shalt open thine hand wide.

Oscar Wilde thought the proper aim is to try and reconstruct society on such a basis that poverty will be impossible, and that charity only prolongs the disease. Do the readings want care for the poor, or an end of poverty, or both?

The cost of a journey was given to the poor instead. When ointment was poured out some said it might have been sold and given to the poor, and Jesus defended the woman. When is the poor’s claim decisive, and when not?
A charitable company, a society, a meeting. Tocqueville on the Americans: of all ages, all conditions, and all dispositions, they constantly form associations.
“Do not let it cease or weaken.” Let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.

A share of the common storehouse is set aside for orphans and the incapacitated. Lay up the tithe within thy gates: and the stranger, and the fatherless, and the widow shall come, and shall eat and be satisfied.
Israel’s older provision left the corners of the field: thou shalt leave them for the poor and stranger.
Establish resources for the weak and the education of orphans. Job’s account of a good life: I was eyes to the blind, and feet was I to the lame; I was a father to the poor.

Helping the poor and orphans is service to the Kingdom. The Qur’an defines righteousness as belief and this: to give wealth, for love of Him, to kinsfolk and to orphans and the needy and the wayfarer.
An Assembly prepared food for the poor. I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
The charitable company must be preserved, “and complete order must be strived for”. Let all things be done decently and in order.
The disciples of Christ, the reading recalls, organized such care. They appointed seven men of honest report over the daily ministration to widows.
When a believer dies in debt, the friends should pay it. If he oweth thee ought, put that on mine account.
Sell the honey and give the proceeds to the poor. He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the Lord.
The Society cares for orphans and comforts the poor. Therefor the orphan oppress not.
A welfare association is founded in a provincial town. At Joppa the widows stood weeping, and shewing the coats and garments which Dorcas made, while she was with them.
Western friends support a school in Persia. That your abundance may be a supply for their want, that their abundance also may be a supply for your want: that there may be equality.
Around the house of worship: an orphans’ school, a college, a hospital, a home for the disabled. The physician’s oath: into whatever houses I enter, I will go for the benefit of the sick.
A temple with these dependencies is worship turned outward. Mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.
A home for the incurable, a home for the poor. I was sick, and ye visited me.

American philanthropy is praised. Thoreau, an American, was unimpressed by it: there are a thousand hacking at the branches of evil to one who is striking at the root. What would striking at the root of poverty be, in the readings’ terms?
Should believers take part in charitable work or attend to spiritual things only? Micah does not separate them: to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God.

All societies working for human betterment are good. Mencius: treat with reverence the elders in your own family, so that the elders in the families of others shall be similarly treated; treat with kindness the young in your own family, and so the young of others.
He will be compelled, for his own happiness, to spend for the community. Marley’s ghost, too late: mankind was my business; the common welfare was my business.
The wealthy end in disappointment unless they spend for others. Carnegie: the man who dies thus rich dies disgraced.
Charge them that are rich in this world, that they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute.

Someone asks whether “charity” is good. Blake: pity would be no more if we did not make somebody poor; and mercy no more could be if all were as happy as we. He suspects charity of needing the misery it relieves. How can a charitable society avoid deserving that suspicion?
Believers are enjoined to look after one another. The Prophet: every one of you is a guardian, and every one of you is responsible for those in his charge.
“Charity to the poor and needy is the best of all deeds.” Is not this the fast that I have chosen: to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house?

Some give quietly to wayfarers and the poor of the city. When thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth. Societies need lists, reports and appeals. What is kept of the secret alms inside an organized charity?

May these philanthropic aims have a great effect. Franklin Roosevelt’s measure: the test of our progress is not whether we add more to the abundance of those who have much; it is whether we provide enough for those who have too little.
Charitable deeds have an effect on the healing of the one who does them. The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.
Benevolence opens the springs of abundance. Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over.

shortfall: Some readings are brief instructions about particular funds and societies, or repeat the same commendation; they share companions.
